suggested_experiment_name: Gamma-ray attenuation (Fermi-LAT + Cherenkov blazar optical depths)
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1 (plot shows log10(g_agamma/GeV^-1); values converted back to linear GeV^-1)
notes: Bernal et al. (arXiv:2208.13794) use gamma-ray optical depth measurements from ~800 blazars (Fermi-LAT + Cherenkov telescopes) to constrain decaying ALP dark matter contributions to the EBL. They report the strongest bounds on g_agamma over the 8-25 eV mass range, improving prior bounds (globular clusters ~6.6e-11 GeV^-1) by up to more than an order of magnitude. A mild 2.1-sigma preference for an ALP signal is found (best fit m_a c^2 = 9.1 eV, Gamma_a = 2.5e-24 s^-1, i.e. g_agamma = 2.1e-11 GeV^-1), interpreted conservatively as an upper bound. No numerical table is provided; the exclusion curve is shown in Fig. 3 (contours in log10(g_agamma) vs log10(m_a c^2)). The data_points above are approximate reconstructions of the 95% CL upper bound anchored to the quoted best-fit values and the stated improvement factors, assuming roughly mass-independent decay-rate sensitivity (g ~ m^-3/2 scaling); hence moderate extraction confidence.
